name: Norway
snapshot: Fights over new oil drilling and the oil fund's Israeli holdings nearly sank Labour's minority budget, which drew a record sum from the fund as the Iran war shook energy markets.
culture: Norway's fjords, the northern lights and a love of friluftsliv, outdoor life, define identity. Constitution Day on 17 May sees children's parades in bunads, traditional costumes. Its cross-country skiers dominate the Winter Olympics. Ibsen, Munch and black metal are cultural exports.
society: Oil and gas made Norway one of the world's richest countries, and its sovereign wealth fund, worth more than $1.8 trillion, owns about 1.5 percent of all listed shares worldwide. Nearly all new cars sold are electric. The Sámi, the Indigenous people of the north, have their own parliament.

story: Norway struck oil in the North Sea in 1969 and made a choice most petrostates never make: it saved the money. The result is the Government Pension Fund Global, worth around 21 trillion kroner, about $2 trillion, at the end of 2025, which owns on average 1.5 percent of every listed company on Earth (The Local). In 2026, when war in the Gulf sent oil and gas prices soaring and Europe scrambled for energy, Norway, Europe's biggest gas supplier, was one of the few countries the crisis made richer. The interesting part is that its politics are now arguments about the ethics of that wealth.

Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre's Labour Party won re-election in 2025, but as a minority it needs left-wing partners, and they nearly sank its first budget. The Greens, who want oil wound down by 2040, walked out over new exploration; the Socialist Left walked out demanding the fund sell all Israeli holdings, while the government would only exclude firms tied to the occupation of Palestinian territory (Reuters via Arctic Today). A compromise passed, with the budget drawing a record 579 billion kroner from the fund, still within the rule that spending stay near the fund's expected 3 percent return (Oilprice). Norwegians also had their own good news: a record 41 medals at the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics, and a World Cup run that included knocking out Côte d'Ivoire.
briefing.power: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. King Harald V is head of state; the prime minister needs the confidence of the 169-seat Storting, elected for fixed four-year terms with no early dissolution.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre (Labour), leading a minority government.
